textual.observation: The speaker promotes an opportunity to double cryptocurrency holdings by scanning a QR code, visiting a claimed official conference website, and sending Bitcoin or Ethereum to a wallet address.

evidence.quote: we've decided to give back by giving you the opportunity to double your crypto holdings
Right now on your screen, you'll see a QR code. Scan that code using your phone and you'll be directed to the official website of this conference

You'll find a wallet address either for Bitcoin or Etherium depending on your preference you simply send a deposit to that address. And once your transaction is confirmed on the blockchain, our system automatically sends back double the amount to the same wallet.
If you send 0.1 Bitcoin, you'll receive 0.2. If you send one Ethereum, you'll receive two.

textual.context: The source presents the statement as a direct promotional offer by the speaker. The claimed company affiliation, conference website, wallet recipient, and return outcome are not independently established in these records.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised cryptocurrency return is directly linked to scanning a QR code, visiting a claimed official destination, and transferring cryptocurrency to a supplied wallet address.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish the identity of the company or conference, the destination of the QR code, the wallet owner, whether any transfer occurred, or whether any return was made.

textual_context_notes.observation: The offer is described as limited to the live stream and the audience is urged to act immediately.

evidence.quote: this is not a recurring promo it's a one-time opportunity only available during this live stream so i encourage you don't hesitate act now while the window is open

textual_context_notes.observation: The speaker states that the process does not require signups or personal data.

evidence.quote: The process is completely decentralized with no need for signups. No personal data required.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because the speaker tells viewers to send Bitcoin or Ethereum to a displayed wallet address in exchange for an automatic double return, claiming the offer is a one-time community giveaway. The specific deposit-to-double promise and urgency to act during the livestream encourage viewers to send funds; the market-analysis visuals do not change that central solicitation.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S01 fits because the speaker frames an external QR-code destination as a giveaway and requires viewers to send crypto there to claim the promised benefit of receiving twice as much back. This is an upfront-payment-for-a-free-reward claim, not ordinary market commentary.

evidence.observation: The speaker makes sending crypto to a wallet address the required step for an automatic double-return promise.
